findings.issue: The catch-all route throws a 404 and renders null; the actual Not-found UI lives in root.tsx (NotFound export) as an ErrorBoundary fallback. The UI for a route is a file away from the route itself, and other routes' 404s silently depend on root.tsx's boundary.
findings.suggestion: Render the Not found UI in routes/not-found.tsx (and/or keep a single shared NotFound component in components/, imported by root's boundary), so the route file owns its output.

findings.issue: The Move API response type is declared independently in routes/pokemon.tsx:44 and routes/move.tsx:8; a change to the API shape (or a fix to a field) must be made twice and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Declare the API record types once in lib/api.server.ts (which already owns TypeRecord/GenerationRecord) or a shared lib/api-types.ts and import them in both routes.

findings.issue: Filter controls are uncontrolled with refs, a manual debounce and two hydration-sync effects; changing filter behavior (adding a control, altering debounce) requires threading refs and both effects correctly, and the empty-deps effect is easy to get wrong.
findings.suggestion: Consider controlled inputs driven from loaderData (or a small useFilters hook) so URL state is the single source and the sync effects disappear.

findings.issue: Default move ordering (level-then-name) is applied in the pokemon.tsx loader while user-driven sorting lives in MoveTable; changing sort semantics touches both, and the 'missing sorts last' rule only exists in the component.
findings.suggestion: Move all ordering (including the default) into MoveTable via an initial sort state, or extract a shared sort helper next to MoveRow.

findings.issue: The generic Card type carries the ability page's `hidden` flag, coupling a shared model and component (PokemonCards.tsx:25) to one feature — the thing that makes Abilities removal leave residue.
findings.suggestion: Keep Card generic and let PokemonCards accept an optional per-card note/extra slot, or move the hidden-ability note to a wrapper used only by the ability route.

findings.issue: pokemonCards' `extra` callback is used via a roundtrip: refs are re-wrapped as {…pokemon, hidden} only for `extra` to unwrap `hidden` again — a clever but confusing API.
findings.suggestion: Type `extra` as (ref: T) => Partial<Card> and pass `ability.pokemon` directly, letting ability.tsx read `ref.is_hidden`.

findings.issue: versionGroupOrders fetches the full version-group endpoint list on every Pokémon page load; it is cached only per-URL (60s TTL), so this whole-endpoint join belongs with the long-lived index in api.server.ts.
findings.suggestion: Add a versionGroup order map to the cached Index in api.server.ts so the pokemon loader just looks it up.

findings.issue: All styles live in one ~650-line file; feature removal or restyling requires grepping for the right class names, though the section comments keep it navigable.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable at this size; if the app grows, split per-route stylesheets imported by each route module (Vite supports this natively).

summary: This is a well-organized, current-idiom React Router v8 app: one server-only data module owns all API and caching concerns, components are small presentational seams, and route modules are consistently shaped and typegen-typed. Bugs and data-source changes land in one obvious place, and every Pokémon-card list and sort interaction flows through a single choke point. The main editability costs are features whose edges leak into shared code (Abilities' hidden flag, the duplicated Move type) and the odd 404 split between root.tsx and not-found.tsx.
